0.reason: the producer is a one-off evidence script under docs/evidence/fragments that writes one record section; reusing reckon/_store.py's evidence-append helper would couple it to product internals for no behaviour gain, so it is not worth a repair round

findings.text: write_archive re-implements the evidence-append capability the repository already owns: reckon/_store.py:1372 `_append_evidence_to_text` with _evidence_section_html, and the marker constants at reckon/evidence.py:81, already insert an anchored <section> carrying data-evidence-origin="append" before </main> and apply the owner's refusals (duplicate anchor, forged body structure, reserved anchors). The producer's regex splice duplicates the insertion rather than extending the owner, so the archive-insertion mechanic now has two implementations that can drift; it does honour the owner's append marker, so a later synthesis carries the section forward. Non-blocking because the producer is a standalone evidence script that must be idempotent on rerun, while the owner refuses a plan that already carries the anchor by design.

LEAD_DECISION names a role in a module-level source symbol, which the repository naming rule forbids (no author or role attribution in symbol names); the constant carries a date, so name it by what it records (e.g. DECISION_DATE). The rendered prose may still say whose decision it was, because that is output data.

the node declared a figure path (docs/figures/workers-spend-fewer-tokens-per-landed-node/pooled-local-record-s8) and no figure was written; the pooled four-arm table with 90% intervals at this line is exactly the comparison the plan's graphics mandate asks a figure to carry (four arms over 18 sections), so a reader must reconstruct the separation from numbers. The done_when names no figure and the archive's earlier sections carry none, so this is a missed illustration rather than a broken measure.
